readers.2:real: From a still, almost self-erasing quiet, something in them suddenly wakes—a hunger to act, to be the one who does it, that pulls them off their first true line. Yet even mid-stray they feel the old steadiness call them back, and they return to a firmer, more righteous footing than the one they left.
readers.0:real: They hold back at first, cheeks warming under any direct gaze, their mind circling a single hope long after others have moved on, until the wanting spills out into words a size too large for the moment. Then, as if catching their own reflection, they fall into a fearless, wanting-nothing silence that suits them far better than the bluster ever did.
readers.0:random: There is a magnetic pull to them, the way iron filings drift toward warmth, yet underneath runs something glacial and contained, a held cold that never quite spills. They move through rooms like vapor finding the open window, settling at last into the wide flat calm of someone who has stopped needing to be anywhere in particular.
readers.6:real: They give in too easily to every pleasure within reach, and from that overflow comes a feverish, racing drive that sharpens into a need to be singular, special, the one who outshines—curdling, finally, into a green ache at anyone who does. But there is a leash they keep learning to hold, and on their better days the envy softens into a strange, generous gladness at others' good fortune.
readers.free:1: They keep their coat buttoned to the throat in any weather, as though the world might be talked out of touching them if they simply present no opening. Yet they remember the birthdays of people who have forgotten theirs, leaving small unsigned kindnesses that everyone suspects and no one can prove.
readers.0:scrambled: Shy to the point of vanishing, they hold a thought past all reason, nursing a fragile hope and then flinching from a fear that the hope invites. In their best moments the shyness hardens into a quiet fearlessness and the hope loosens into letting-go, though the self that wants and worries is never far beneath.
readers.5:random: There is a banked heat in them, glowing low, that someone could blow back into flame with a single word, though long silences leave them gone glacial and far. They hold their shape like set stone, returning always to that first ember, the warm coal at the center they never quite let go cold.
readers.3:random: They draw things to themselves and then go slack, pulled by tides they don't name, rising like scaffolding only to drift loose again. Something in them keeps thinning toward vapor, as if the marrow of who they are were always quietly leaving the room.
readers.2:scrambled: They perform a virtue they don't quite own, building a self that insists on its own specialness while losing the thread of what actually matters. On the days they soften, the pretense gives way to a plain straightforwardness and the muddle resolves into something like conscience—yet the doer, the one who must be seen doing, lingers.
readers.7:real: They throw themselves into motion, then into thought, then into a strange wish to undo it all, shrinking shy before circling back to a fresh-minted clarity that curdles, at the edges, into envy. But the action knows how to become stillness, the undoing-wish turns toward life, and on a good day the envy ripens into honest gladness for another's joy.
readers.free:0: They speak in the cadence of someone always half-listening for an interruption that rarely comes, leaving sentences open like doors. Their hands betray them—forever tidying the edges of things, aligning a fork, a stack of papers, the hem of a stranger's untucked thought.
readers.1:scrambled: They live much of their life in a dimmed inner room, heavy-lidded, the doing-self insisting on its weight while a deep drowsiness pulls them under again and again. But the darkness in them is the kind that can turn to knowing, and the heavy sleep keeps trembling, always, on the verge of waking.
readers.5:real: They let go of things before they are ready, calling it freedom, then swing into a fierce will to build and provide that can sharpen, on bad days, into a hardness toward the weak and a sour envy of the lucky. Still, the letting-go keeps reaching toward something more like true release, and the envy, when they tend it, can soften into gladness at another's good.
readers.4:random: They come in like a tide, generous and overflowing, then fasten down hard, riveted in place, before thinning toward the vague and vaporous. What lasts is the cobble of them—plain, set, underfoot—a stone that still remembers, faintly, the warmth it once held.
readers.7:random: They fasten onto a thing the way a rivet bites, then drift glacial and remote, raising tall ambitions like girders before scattering loose again. But the fixing instinct keeps wanting to become a beacon, and beneath all the wandering they stay cobbled and solid, a banked warmth waiting just under the cold.
readers.2:random: They lock onto a single point until it pixelates into too much detail, then snap shut around it like a socket gripping its plug. Whatever they hold keeps thinning toward vapor, slipping out through the marrow even as their grip tightens.
readers.3:scrambled: They lose the thread of what matters while busying themselves with provision and gain, performing a goodness they don't feel and clenching tighter the more uncertain they grow. readers.free:2: They laugh a beat before the joke lands, as if they've heard it all in some earlier life and are only being polite. Strangers tell them secrets in elevators, drawn by a face that promises to forget everything kindly the moment the doors open.
readers.3:real: They drift off their truest line, reaching for a tidy closure that isn't theirs to give, then sink into a wish to undo what they've made even as they insist on being someone uniquely set apart. readers.1:real: They surrender too readily to comfort and appetite, and from that softness a sharper awareness keeps trying to surface, edged with a quick, snappish irritability at every small friction. readers.7:scrambled: They let go too soon, then hold attention with a clenched, dogged grip, dressing a borrowed virtue over a deep shyness and an insistent need to be the one who does. readers.5:scrambled: There is a cruel streak in them that can wound for the pleasure of it, even as a fresh clarity keeps surfacing alongside a strange wish to annihilate the very self that wants and snaps. readers.4:scrambled: They mean to provide and to do good, yet a hardness toward the vulnerable keeps creeping in, propped up by a self that insists on its own central importance and frays into quick irritation. readers.4:real: They are forever closing things off, sealing the chapter, driven by a restless overdrive that, in its rare quiet, lets a clearer awareness rise—an awareness that too often curls into envy of those who seem to have arrived. Still, that envy keeps being turned, gently, into a real gladness at another's good fortune.
readers.6:random: They run cold and far at first, glacial and thinning toward vapor, then fasten down with sudden conviction before drifting loose again. The glacier in them keeps wanting to soften into open tundra, and what endures is the cobblestone solidity underfoot, plain and warm at the core.
readers.1:random: They move with the slow cold of something vast and unhurried, thinning at the edges into mist, yet humming with a buried engine that never quite stops turning. readers.6:scrambled: They carry a darkness they half-believe is just how they are, the doing-self crowding out the light, with a cruel edge and a tendency to clamp down tight when threatened, fraying into irritability. readers.0:real: They hover at the edge of every room, blushing and turning a single thought over and over until it swells into a bright hope they cannot help overstating to anyone who listens. readers.0:random: There is something polarized and pulling about them, drawing loose things into a slow, cold orbit before they harden into a single quiet alignment. They hollow out to receive whatever connects to them, then dissolve into a wide, level openness, more mist than mineral.
readers.6:real: Appetite drives them first, a hunger that flares into restless, overdriven motion as they carve out a self too sharply and resent whatever others hold. readers.free:1: They keep a tidy ledger of every kindness ever done to them and pay each one back twice over, as though warmth were a debt that could be settled. People mistake their generosity for ease, never guessing how carefully it is counted out.
readers.0:scrambled: Shy to the point of vanishing, they hold a single thought with patient attention until it blooms into hope, then teeter at the brink of fear. readers.5:random: A banked heat lives in them, cooling to ice and stiffening into hard upright shapes before thinning to vapor and settling like scattered stone. Always, though, the warmth returns, the loose ground gathering itself back into a low, steady glow.
readers.3:random: They draw the world toward them and let it pull away in turns, like a tide rising and falling around some tall, fixed scaffolding inside. Beneath the motion runs a deep marrow-steadiness that finally lets them drift, dissolving softly into open air.
readers.2:scrambled: They wear a borrowed face, sharpening a self they only half believe in while blurring every line between true and false. Pressed hard enough, the mask slips into plain honesty, and the fog clears into a quiet, insistent conscience.
readers.7:real: They move and think in restless succession, undoing themselves between thoughts, flushing with shyness even as fresh awareness keeps being born in them, all shadowed by a low envy. readers.free:0: They speak slowly, as if each sentence were a stone they were setting carefully into a wall only they can see. Strangers find them aloof; the few who stay discover a patience that has simply been waiting, all along, to be trusted.
readers.1:scrambled: A heaviness sits over them like a closed room, the self pressing forward even as a deep drowsy inertia keeps pulling them under. But the dark in them is the kind that yearns toward light, and the long sleep is only the held breath before an awakening they can already sense.
readers.5:real: They let go of things too soon, mistaking flight for freedom, swinging between a will to provide and a streak of coldness, while new understanding and a thread of envy rise together in them. readers.4:random: They surge and recede like water around small fixed points, thinning to mist before settling into scattered, modest stone. Even cooled and broken, a low heat waits in them, ready to glow.

readers.3:real: They drift from where they began, reach a sense of closure, then quietly unmake themselves and sharpen the self anew, all under the sign of something just being born.
